quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When you see a car with very bright headlights coming toward you, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car comes toward you with high beams on, look away from the headlights. Instead, look toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing where the warning signals are flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you must stop. Stay at least 15 feet away from the nearest rail. Also watch for other warning signs, like lowered crossing gates or the sound of an approaching train.

questions.question: You are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough room to cross completely. Never try to pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey above all others?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions override all signs, signals, and road markings. Police officers, fire police, work zone flag persons, and school crossing guards are all authorized to direct traffic.

questions.question: You see an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Squeeze between them.
Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.
Pass the bicyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: When facing multiple hazards, deal with one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then, when it is safe, pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: You see a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon with two solid red lights. What must you do?

options.text: Continue with caution.
Stop, then proceed with caution.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop completely and let pedestrians cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and let pedestrians cross.
questions.explanation: A Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon helps pedestrians cross safely. It only works when a pedestrian activates it. When it shows two solid red lights, you must stop and yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: Before you pass another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and blind spots before passing. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Return to your original lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Cars turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign works with a traffic signal. It tells drivers that when turning left on a green light, they do not have the right-of-way. They must wait for oncoming traffic to clear before turning.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When road or weather conditions are not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Slow down when the road is wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when any condition is not ideal. Even if you drive within the speed limit, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.
You are approaching a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Orange signs mean:

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you that workers are on or near the road. These signs are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop at every red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when:

options.text: You have to stop quickly.
You are passing another car.
You have lost control of your car.
You are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn when you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to stay away from you.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights approaches you, move to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Less dangerous.
Just as safe.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as far, headlight glare can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when changing lanes, entering traffic from a parking space, and when passing other vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before passing to ensure no oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before passing. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate them.
Flash your lights.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate them.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and back. Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs prepare you for road hazards. This sign warns of curves ahead. Slow down and be ready to turn.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Not worry about how many tracks to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains when approaching railroad tracks. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same once you are on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers from both directions can pass.
No passing is allowed.
You can pass if you are on top of a hill.
You can pass during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, what must a driver do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
Give them the right-of-way only when they have the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what. Drivers must always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally.

questions.question: You want to turn at an intersection but you are not in the correct lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your signal and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely move into the correct lane, then back up to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. Go to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Solid and broken yellow combined
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-way road means no one can cross it to pass.
